target.title: fix(gateway): keep channels responsive after startup requests finish
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channels started or restarted from a short-lived gateway transaction could stop accepting later work after that transaction finished. Provider callbacks, approval handlers, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel manager now uses the existing process-lifetime admission boundary when it creates approval-bootstrap work, the provider task, and the tracked cleanup/recovery/restart reaction chain. Keeping the boundary in the lifecycle owner covers RPC starts, startup, health recovery, hot reload, and future callers without weakening real restart or suspension fences.

The change builds on current `main`: recent SecretRef owner isolation, gateway-native approval context, plugin HTTP route registry, stop-timeout recovery, terminal-disconnect handling, and restart accounting remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain responsive after the request or reload transaction that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still close admission normally.

## Evidence

- RED on current `main` before the fix: the three focused lifecycle cases failed with provider `true` vs `false`, approval `true` vs `false`, and automatic restart `[false, true]` vs `[false, false]`.
- Exact final head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 178/178 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed on the exact final head.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed before the final conflict-free rebase; the exact-head focused suites above cover all changed and sibling admission paths.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files — passed on the exact final head.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh independent review found no Critical, Important, or Minor findings and judged the channel manager to be the correct bounded owner boundary.

### Redacted real-environment transcript

Source: real hosted Kubernetes tenant logs captured on 2026-07-18 UTC. Tenant, pod, instance, user, bot, chat, message, update, session, UUID, domain, config hash, and user-content fields are removed. The running production image was pre-fix, so this section is explicitly a real-environment reproduction and restart recovery control; it is not represented as execution of this PR head.

Tenant A reproduced the request-lifetime leak after a combined model and Telegram policy patch:

```text
05:57:57 [gateway] config.patch ... changedPaths=agents.defaults.model.primary,channels.telegram.dmPolicy restartReason=config.patch
05:57:57 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete
05:57:58 [gateway/channels] channel restart cancelled by config supersession or restart
05:57:58 [reload] config reload failed: GatewayHotReloadCancelledError: config hot reload cancelled by config supersession or in-process restart
05:57:58 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
05:57:58 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.telegram.dmPolicy, agents.defaults.model.primary)
05:58:00 [telegram] webhook local listener started
05:58:15 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=telegram outcome=error error="GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted"
05:58:15 [telegram] webhook spooled update <redacted> failed; keeping for retry attempt 2/8: GatewayDrainingError
```

Tenant B independently reproduced the same boundary failure with a Telegram-policy-only patch:

```text
05:43:50 [reload] config change detected (channels.telegram.dmPolicy)
05:43:50 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete
05:43:50 [gateway/channels] channel restart cancelled by config supersession or restart
05:43:50 [reload] config reload failed: GatewayHotReloadCancelledError
05:43:50 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
05:43:50 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.telegram.dmPolicy)
06:02:58 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=telegram outcome=error error="GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted"
06:02:59 [telegram] webhook spooled update <redacted> failed; keeping for retry attempt 2/8
```

Across the retained previous-container logs:

- Tenant A: 572 terminal Telegram processing errors and 572 durable spool retries after one cancelled channel restart.
- Tenant B: 83 terminal Telegram processing errors and 83 durable spool retries after one cancelled channel restart.
- A third tenant recorded the same cancelled-restart sequence but had no post-trigger Telegram ingress; ordinary Gateway RPC and the webhook listener remained available, so those health signals did not prove the long-lived channel context could admit work.

Process-restart recovery control:

```text
07:47:36 [gateway] signal SIGTERM received
07:47:36 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
07:47:37 [shutdown] started: gateway stopping
07:47:37 [shutdown] completed cleanly

07:47:39 [gateway] signal SIGTERM received
07:47:39 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
07:47:39 [shutdown] started: gateway stopping
07:47:40 [shutdown] completed cleanly
```

After the containers restarted in place, the two tenants with pending ingress recorded 17 and 4 terminal `message processed ... outcome=completed` events respectively, with zero new `GatewayDrainingError` lines. The third tenant had no pending ingress and zero draining errors.

Exact PR-head focused test transcript:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       161 passed (161)

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards
```

AI-assisted change. Private incident details were excluded; the redacted transcript above retains only behaviorally relevant runtime events.
